elements.description:
Whether trust in an AI matches its performance: a reliance–accuracy dial with its trend, signals against review
thresholds, overtrust and undertrust episodes, and the recommended review level.

properties.name: heading
properties.description: The heading, and the region's name

properties.name: scope
properties.description: What the numbers cover, a quiet line under the heading – e.g. "Last 30 days · 412 answers"

properties.name: index
properties.description: The reliance–accuracy index, 0–1 (1: trust matches accuracy). Unset, it is 1 − |reliance − accuracy|

properties.name: reliance
properties.description: How often people relied on the AI's output, 0–1 – compared with `accuracy` to say which way trust leans

properties.name: accuracy
properties.description: How often the AI's output was right, 0–1

properties.name: trend
properties.description: The index over recent windows, oldest first – drawn as the trend line

properties.name: calibratedAt
properties.description: Index from which the dial reads "Calibrated" (0–1)

properties.name: driftAt
properties.description: Index from which the dial reads "Drifting"; below it, "Miscalibrated" (0–1)

properties.name: signals
properties.description: Behaviour signals, each a 0–1 value where higher means more reason to review

properties.name: spotCheckAt
properties.description: Signal value from which a spot-check is recommended (0–1)

properties.name: mandatoryAt
properties.description: Signal value from which review of every output is recommended (0–1)

properties.name: overtrust
properties.description: Overtrust episodes: output relied on, then found wrong

properties.name: undertrust
properties.description: Undertrust episodes: output overridden, then found right

properties.name: browsable
properties.description: The episode counts are buttons that fire tc-episodes-open

properties.name: reviewLevel
properties.description: The review level in force – when it differs from the recommendation, the footer offers to switch

properties.name: recommended
properties.description: Overrides the recommended level worked out from the signals and the index

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Overrides the sentence that explains the recommendation

properties.name: levelLabels
properties.description: Names of the review levels

properties.name: domains
properties.description: The calibration table: one row per domain, the AI's accuracy against the confidence it stated; empty hides it

properties.name: calibrationTolerance
properties.description: How far confidence may sit from accuracy (0–1) and still read "Well calibrated"

properties.name: calibrationLabels
properties.description: The names of the calibration bands – in place of Well calibrated, Over-confident and Under-confident

properties.name: domainsLabel
properties.description: The calibration table's caption

properties.name: agents
properties.description: Agents to rank by the rating the app gives each; empty hides the ranking

properties.name: agentsLabel
properties.description: The ranking's caption

properties.name: locale
properties.description: Locale for numbers

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-review-level-change
events.description: The footer's switch was pressed ({ level, reviewLevel, previous }: RelianceReviewLevelChange – reviewLevel is the new level); cancelable – prevent it to keep `reviewLevel` yourself

events.name: tc-episodes-open
events.description: An episode count was pressed, with `browsable` set (detail: { kind: "overtrust" | "undertrust" })

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, and the region's name

props.name: reviewLevel
props.description:
The review level in force. Controlled when defined: pair with onReviewLevelChange and pass the new level back.
Otherwise the component keeps it, starting from `defaultReviewLevel`

props.name: defaultReviewLevel
props.description: The level in force at first, when uncontrolled – leave both unset for no footer

props.name: onReviewLevelChange
props.description: The footer's switch was pressed: the new level and the one before

props.name: onOpenEpisodes
props.description: Makes the episode counts buttons; called with the kind pressed

changelog: **Event details:** four change events gained a field named after the property they change. The existing fields stay. The docs' controlled examples read these names, which the events lacked; the new Angular type check caught it. - `tc-artifact-panel`'s `tc-selected-change`: `selected`. - `tc-email-draft`'s `tc-recipient-change`: `recipient`. - `tc-reliance-gauge`'s `tc-review-level-change`: `reviewLevel`. - `tc-transcript-review`'s `tc-translation-mode-change`: `translationMode`.

**Trust & calibration**, from THEMIS and built domain-neutral: - claims and their reliability: `tc-claim-answer`, `tc-verification-queue`, `tc-reflection-gate`, `tc-reliance-gauge`, `tc-disagreement-banner`, `tc-synthesis-notes`; - where outputs came from: `tc-lineage-graph`, `tc-validity-badge`, `tc-provenance-summary`, `tc-correction-propagation`, `tc-attestation-check`, `tc-run-manifest`; - policy and control: `tc-policy-simulator`, `tc-gate-config`, `tc-coverage-matrix`, `tc-kill-switch`, `tc-playbook-canvas`.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: :has()
features.why: Layout and state that depend on what's inside a part (an icon present, a focused field).

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.
